chapter: Small group, new sound and Europe
title: A family again, and long stays at Birdland
summary: After Foster and Wess the band got back into a family groove, with long Birdland stays.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: There's one thing I'd like to comment on in any of the bands which, of course, it is Basie -- basically is responsible for it -- isn't he? I mean, with as many changes, you know -- with as many different bands as there have been -- every time we hear the band -- we always say the same thing. It always looks like the guys are enjoying
themselves.
Mm hmm.
Which is a really surprising thing when as -- for instance -- when we say -- alright -- Marshall came in and things got different -- things got more serious.
Mm hmm. Mm hmm.
The musicians were more schooled maybe -- like Frank Wess, and all those things.
Mm hmm. Mm hmm.
And, yet as you watch a performance -- no matter who's up there in those or whatever it is -- guys are enjoying themselves -- year after year -- and decade after decade.
Well, you know, we got kind of back as a family thing after we -- you know -- after we got Frank Foster and Frank Wess.
Oh, you did?
Yeah. We got back into a family groove, during that period.
Oh, you did.
You know, during that period. Like the Birdland City, -- you know -- when we were in Birdland --everybody was -- really -- the Birdland thing was --
How many years were you playing sort of in and out of Birdland? I mean, quite a long time?
Quite a long spell. A long time, and we spent an awful lot of time in Birdland. We used to go in there and spend four weeks -- six weeks, you know. Sitting back in one spot and just
really enjoying ourselves, you know.
Yeah. Yeah.
Being able to sit down in one spot.
Yeah. And, in New York.
And, in New York, you know. And, the place is like this every night, more or less -- you know.
Yeah. Yeah.
It was really a beautiful thing for us -- and the way the band sounded in there, you know. And, the personnel.
Yeah. It's a shame there's no place in New York.
It's a shame that that place -- you know -- because that was it.
That's a terrible shame.

It really is. That was the only place -- you know -- we had to do. We used to go over to the Waldorf and do [---] you know. Maybe five weeks, four weeks, whatever -- then come right back over to Birdland and stay in there for -- like -- three and four weeks, you know. Then go out of town and then come right back into Birdland -- you know. It was --
Where your own public could get at you.
Oh, yeah. Yeah. It was something else. It's a shame.
When -- what was that -- the late '50's? Do you know, Stan?
Through the '50's and into the '60's.
Right. Into the '60's. It went into the '60's.
Yeah.
Into the early '60's, right?
